filo tag FILE... TAG...
filo untag FILE... TAG...

  Gives each file the tags, or removes them. A tag is key:value (sender:British
  Gas, project:house sale) or a bare value (urgent); a file can have any number,
  and several values for one key. The files come first: the arguments that are
  on the disk are files, and the first that is not starts the tags, so quote a
  tag with spaces. A tag that is also the name of something in the current
  directory is read as a file: run filo from another directory.

  Spelling: the first colon ends the key when what is before it is letters,
  digits, - and _ with a letter (10:30 call is a bare tag). Keys are lower case;
  values keep the case first typed, and match in any case: once a file has
  sender:British Gas, sender:british gas gives another file the same tag (filo
  tags rename changes the spelling). Spaces in a value are trimmed and runs of
  them made one. A tag cannot hold ; or *, and needs a value: sender: alone is a
  search, or for untag every value of the key.

  All or nothing: if any file cannot be tagged (a directory, a symlink, outside
  every root, skipped by its root's settings), nothing changes and every refusal
  is listed. A file filo has not seen yet is registered by itself first, taking
  the tags of any copies of its content; one that looks moved from a file the
  register has is refused until filo scan pairs them.

  Tags follow the file through moves and edits, and a new copy of a tagged file
  takes its tags. Find files by tag with filo find --tag; many files at once
  with filo export and filo update.
